text:
alex: heads up — getting a spike of 502/504s hitting the hosted inference endpoint via edge in us-west-2 around 08:43 UTC. multiple customers reporting timeouts and failed generations. @jordan_support can you coord with affected accounts?

jordan_support: saw this too, customer_emily opened a ticket. they get 502s on long requests and 504s intermittently. provided a quick repro curl. will share below.

alex: repro curl (from support laptop):
```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-open-13b\",\"input\":\"<long prompt ~2k tokens>\"}'
```

alex: response: 502 Bad Gateway or connection reset, sometimes an nginx 504 with header `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 15000` then timeout.

online: deploy-bot: alert: hosted-api-edge-us-west-2-high-5xx-rate triggered at 2026-03-15T08:44:10Z :rotating_light:

tony_sre: looking at envoy logs on the edge pool — seeing `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `no healthy upstream` in a few proxies. frequent `503` from connection pool, then NGINX returns 502.

li_infra: I pulled the admin `/clusters` output, there's an unhealthy backend set for the inference-target group. cluster stats show high `cx_overflow` and `upstream_connection_failure`.

li_infra: snippet from envoy stderr (08:44:12):
```
[2026-03-15T08:44:12.123Z] [warning] envoy upstream reset: reason=connection_failure, host=10.0.42.9:8080, message=connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T08:44:12.124Z] [error] no healthy upstream for cluster inference-target-usw2
```

alex: seems like backend inference hosts are dropping long-lived streaming connections during heavy token generation. p95 token generation time jumped from ~300ms to >5s for some requests.

jordan_support: customer_emily logs show repeated `ECONNRESET` and then the SDK retries but hits rate limits so multiple attempts cascade. I've told them to backoff and added a temporary retry-window suggestion.

tony_sre: quick triage steps I ran:
- checked LB health checks (tcp keepalive ok)
- verified autoscaler didn't spin new backend pods because CPU thresholds were at 95% but pod startup was slow due to image pull backlog
- noticed a config change pushed at 06:12 UTC that reduced `max_connections` on the upstream pool from 200 -> 80 (candidate cause)

li_infra: that config change was from a recent proxy tuning PR (internal ref: infra/proxy#812) — it was intended to reduce memory usage but the canary exposed lower capacity. I have the PR number and who merged it.

alex: @li_infra can we roll back that change in canary immediately and broaden capacity? If not, spin a temporary autoscale policy to allow burst to 300 connections.

li_infra: I'm prepping a rollback patch now. also opening a hotfix to revert `max_connections` and bump healthcheck rate for the inference pool.

deploy-bot: prod deploy rollback started for infra/proxy@infra/proxy#812 at 08:52:03Z

tony_sre: mitigation while rollback lands:
- route traffic away from the smallest canary pool via service weight adjustments (will shift to older healthy proxies)
- increase per-route timeout to avoid NGINX 504s for in-flight long gen requests (temporary)

jordan_support: I sent an update to customer_emily: apologies, temporary capacity issue, recommended retry/backoff and suggested using a shorter prompt if possible. customer accepted workaround and asked for ETA.

alex: timeline — rollback should finish within 6–8 minutes from start. I'll monitor for 5xx rate drop and p95 token latency.

li_infra: rollback completed at 08:58:40Z. I also bumped `max_connections` back to 250 and scaled the inference-target pool by +4 instances as a stopgap.

tony_sre: post-rollback metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 7.8% -> 0.9% over 5 minutes; p95 token gen back to ~340ms. Monitoring for any regressions.

jordan_support: updated customer_emily with mitigation and ETA, will follow up with a timeline for root cause once we confirm stability. they said they can wait for two business days.

alex: root cause hypothesis: proxy config change reduced upstream concurrent connections causing connection saturation under bursty long-running streaming requests; combined with slower pod startups/autoscaler headroom led to short window with no healthy upstreams.

li_infra: action items:
- revert/properly test proxy tuning and add load test sim with long streaming workloads (owner: li_infra)
- increase canary observation window and include p95 token latency as a gating metric (owner: tony_sre)
- tweak autoscaler cooldown/startup grace to prefer spinning fast warm instances for inference (owner: infra-autoscale team)
- provide customer-facing incident summary and ETA (owner: jordan_support)

tony_sre: I'll also add more telemetry on `x-envoy-upstream-service-time` and `cx_overflow` to alert earlier.

jordan_support: creating support ticket note and linking this thread. assigning follow-up to alex for postmortem.

customer_emily: thanks for the fast response — appreciate the workaround. please keep me posted. :thumbsup:

alex: will draft postmortem once metrics stabilize. marking this thread resolved for support until we have RCA. :white_check_mark:
